title: Data Structures & Algorithms in Go
intro: Data structures and algorithms interview questions in Go test both your CS fundamentals and your knowledge of Go's standard library. This module covers Big-O complexity for Go's built-in operations (slice append amortised O(1), map lookup/insert O(1), len() O(1) for slices and maps), implementing a stack and queue using a slice (Go has no built-in stack/queue — slices serve both roles with append and slice re-assignment), implementing a singly linked list as a Go struct, sorting with sort.Slice (the comparator function) and sort.Strings / sort.Ints for common cases, binary search with sort.Search, the two-pointer pattern for array problems (written idiomatically in Go), and hash map patterns for frequency counting and two-sum style problems. Every answer shows the complete, runnable Go code the interviewer expects — not pseudocode, not Python with Go syntax bolted on, but idiomatic Go using range, multiple assignment, and the standard library tools Go developers actually reach for.
